subject: TritonGear — integration gating: reference architecture & acceptance plan
messages:
From: Calvin R. Hayes <calvin@tritongear.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Nisha Patel <nisha@tritongear.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: TritonGear — Redwood integration gating: reference architecture and test plan

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at TritonGear is excited to move toward a gated acceptance with Redwood. Attached is a short integration spec that summarizes our current integration approach (tg-integration-spec.pdf).

High level asks from our side:
- Confirm Redwood’s recommended reference architecture for a low-latency inference flow when calling model endpoints from our edge services.
- Identify required telemetry and trace headers so we can include them in our test harness.
- Agree on an acceptance test matrix and who owns each test.

We’re aiming to start the acceptance window the week of May 10. Can you point us to the right folks on the Redwood side for architecture sign-off and the actual test execution?

Appreciate it — I’ve CC’d Nisha (engineering) who will help coordinate artifacts from our side.

—Calvin
Calvin R. Hayes
Head of Platform Engineering, TritonGear Inc.
calvin@tritongear.com

Attachment: tg-integration-spec.pdf (summary spec, 6 pages)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Calvin R. Hayes <calvin@tritongear.com>
Cc: Nisha Patel <nisha@tritongear.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TritonGear — Redwood integration gating: reference architecture & acceptance plan

Calvin,

Thanks — I reviewed the spec and it looks like a good starting point. I’m looping in Sergio (runtime/ops) and Laura (solutions) to scope the validation steps. Quick questions to help us size the runbook:

1) Traffic profile: can you share expected qps and p95 target latency from edge to model (<ms)?
2) Payloads: please attach representative sample payloads (size distribution + few edge-cases).
3) Auth and routing: will Triton use mTLS or a proxy with token-based auth? Any SSO/OAuth integration for admin UX?
4) Telemetry: which headers/traces do you want propagated (correlation-id, span-id, customer-id)?

We’ll prepare a Redwood integration checklist (I’ll attach the template) and propose owners for each gating step (architecture sign-off, canary run, performance test, security scan). Can Sergio and Laura own the runbook and canary plan respectively?

I’ll send a proposed schedule by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Partner Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (template)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: TritonGear gating — proposed division of work

Sergio/Laura — quick internal plan so we’re aligned before responding to TritonGear:

- Architecture sign-off (Sergio): review their diagram, confirm routing options (direct API vs. private peering), and call out recommended KV-cache sizing and batching params for their expected payloads.
- Canary and acceptance tests (Laura): own canary plan, test matrix, and success criteria. Laura to coordinate test window with Triton.
- Tooling & preflight (Priyom): ensure CI harness (Jenkins/GH actions) can run their payloads and validate model outputs. Add automated failure alerts to our observability.
- Security checklist: ask for token rotation policy and where audit logs live; if they need SOC2 evidence we’ll engage security.

I’ll send the schedule to Calvin tomorrow. Sergio — can you take the reference architecture review and send back notes by EOD Thu? Laura — can you draft a canary plan template and attach to the reply?

Thanks,
Kimberly

On a process note — keep replies short and action-oriented; Triton prefers concrete owners and dates.

From: Calvin R. Hayes <calvin@tritongear.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Nisha Patel <nisha@tritongear.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TritonGear — Redwood integration gating: reference architecture & acceptance plan

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround. Answers below and I’ve attached our current test artifacts (tg-testplan-v1.zip) which contains payload samples, expected-response schemas, and our internal performance baseline.

- Traffic profile: expected steady-state 150 qps with spikes to ~600 qps during peak batch windows. Target p95 (edge-to-model-return) is 1200ms.
- Payloads: attached in /payloads/ — typical size 8KB median, 55KB 95th. Includes long-context prompts and several malformed cases to test robustness.
- Auth/routing: initial integration will use token-based auth to Redwood’s hosted API; longer-term we want to evaluate private peering and mTLS for Dedicated deployments.
- Telemetry: we can propagate correlation-id, customer-id, span-id. We’ll include service.version header for canary detection.

Next steps: we can start a five-day canary beginning May 12. I’ll assign our SRE (Nisha) as the primary contact for the test window. Please confirm Redwood owners and an initial runbook by Friday.

Thanks — attaching tg-testplan-v1.zip (payloads, schema, perf baseline).

—Calvin
Calvin R. Hayes
Head of Platform Engineering, TritonGear Inc.

Attachment: tg-testplan-v1.zip (includes payloads/, expected-responses.json, perf-baseline.csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Calvin R. Hayes <calvin@tritongear.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TritonGear — Redwood integration gating: reference architecture & acceptance plan

Calvin/Nisha — thanks for the details and the test artifacts. We’re aligned to proceed with the gated acceptance. Summary and owners below: 

1) Architecture sign-off (owner: Sergio Alvarez) — deliverable: annotated reference diagram with routing recommendation (hosted vs. dedicated) and cache/batch params. Due: 2027-05-09 EOD.
2) Test harness readiness (owner: Priyom Das) — deliverable: GH Actions pipeline + sample-run job using their payloads. Smoke tests must run in <10m and produce a results artifact. Due: 2027-05-10 EOD.
3) Canary run & validation (owner: Laura Bennett) — 5-day canary starting 2027-05-12. Success criteria: correctness match rate >= 98% against expected-responses.json, p95 model latency <= 1400ms at Triton’s stated qps.
4) Observability & alerts (owner: Kimberly Park) — ensure correlation-id propagation and dashboard links.

Please confirm these owners and dates. I’ve created a shared drive folder and a Jira ticket for tracking: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cTr1tonGear-Redwood and JIRA:TGTG-1123. I’m attaching the canary runbook template we’ll use.

Calvin — if that looks good we’ll kick off the preflight on Monday and aim to start the canary on Wed (May 12).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: canary-runbook.md (canary steps and playbook)
